h1: Playground Slide Materials Compared: Plastic, Steel and FRP

props.title: Playground Slide Materials Compared: Plastic, Steel and FRP
props.summaryText: Which slide material lasts longest and suits Indian weather best: roto-moulded plastic, stainless steel and fibreglass compared, plus how to choose the slide height and shape.
props.author: rohan-mehta
props.imageAlt: Pink plastic slide and climbing wall on artificial turf at a township playground

takeaways.text: Roto-moulded polyethylene is the most common and practical slide material for Indian playgrounds.
Stainless steel slides are very durable but get hot in direct sun, so they need shade or a north-facing position.
FRP slides are rigid and repairable but can crack and their surface can chalk over time.
Choose slide height by age: about 3 ft for toddlers, 5 ft for primary children, 7 ft and above for older children.

faq.q: What is the most popular slide material for durability and fun?
faq.a: Roto-moulded polyethylene is the most widely used slide material because it is durable, seamless, colourful and can be moulded into wave, spiral and tube shapes. Stainless steel is extremely durable but heats up in direct sun.

faq.q: Are metal slides safe in India?
faq.a: Stainless steel slides are strong and long lasting, but in direct sun they can become hot enough to burn skin. If you choose one, place it in shade or facing north, and check the surface temperature on hot days.

faq.q: What height of slide is right for my playground?
faq.a: Around 3 ft for toddlers and preschoolers, 5 ft for primary-age children, and 7 ft or more for older children. Taller slides need a larger safety zone and thicker surfacing.

faq.q: Why do plastic slides cause static shocks?
faq.a: Friction between clothing and plastic builds static charge, especially in dry weather. It is usually harmless, but children with cochlear implants should avoid plastic slides; metal slides or a grounded option are better for them.
